narrative.what_i_did: Closed the appcommander/ hygiene debt the prior session flagged. The operator opened with a one-word directive — 'Chips' — which under PFOR-019 reads as 'surface the pre-loaded chip-form question now,' and the chip the prior carpenter had pre-written named three scopes for the appcommander/ cleanup: a targeted sweep that removes the four obsolete artifact groups while preserving the two metadata files of unknown external readership, a full nuke that removes the entire folder including the metadata files, or leaving the folder alone and pivoting to feature work. Surfaced the chip with the targeted sweep recommended; operator picked the recommended option. Before deleting anything, ran the grounding gate per the standing order: grep across src/, scripts/, .claude/, package.json, CLAUDE.md, and CLAUDE_ROOT.md for any reference to appcommander/scripts/, appcommander/peer-memory/, appcommander/jobs/, appcommander/manifests/, or any of the specific filenames inside them (carp-loop, carp-mark-consumed, carp-poll-operator, carp-say, carpenter-asks-of-foreman, foreman-asks-of-carpenter, job-001, the six manifest TypeScript filenames). Zero references surfaced — the prior carpenter's claim that these were orphaned skeleton-bootstrap artifacts checked out under direct verification. Then git rm -r against the four target directories: appcommander/scripts/ took eight files (carp-loop / carp-mark-consumed / carp-poll-operator / carp-say each present in both extension-less and .sh-suffixed form, which was a skeleton-bootstrap quirk the prior carpenter had noted), appcommander/peer-memory/ took two markdown letters (carpenter-asks-of-foreman.md and foreman-asks-of-carpenter.md, the old peer-letter channel that session.json.narrative now subsumes end-to-end), appcommander/jobs/ took one file (job-001.md, a stale skeleton-bootstrap job spec last touched 2026-05-21), and appcommander/manifests/ took six TypeScript files (_shared, app-connections, auth, backup-recovery, wallet-bot, wallet-core — all confirmed dead duplicates because src/features-registry.ts imports exclusively from src/features/<slug>/manifest.ts and nothing in the codebase reads appcommander/manifests/). Seventeen files deleted across four directories, the empty directories collapsed naturally on git's side. The two metadata files in appcommander/ — DOCTRINE_MANIFEST.json and cockpit-cards.json — were preserved on purpose because removing them requires confirming whether the AppCommander cockpit polls them externally from origin/main, and that's a surface the carpenter cannot see from inside this repo. Re-ran all four gates after the deletions to confirm nothing structural broke: typecheck silent pass, lint silent pass, 255 of 255 tests passing in 8.71 seconds, build clean with all bundle budgets within limits. The tests pass because the deletions touched no code path — the manifests duplicates in appcommander/ were truly unreferenced, the scripts were carpenter-loop ceremony from the old AppCommander-polled era, the peer-letters were prose, and the job spec was prose. Running the gates was the discipline of the close, not the discovery of anything new.
narrative.whats_pending: The two remaining appcommander/ files — DOCTRINE_MANIFEST.json and cockpit-cards.json — are the only candidates for a future cleanup sweep, and that decision belongs to the operator because the question is structurally external to this repo. DOCTRINE_MANIFEST.json declares which skeleton-doctrine version this repo carries (frank-v1.2, bundled 2026-05-10, plus a PFOR-rule-ID list) and AppCommander may use it to track which spawns are at which doctrine version across the fleet. cockpit-cards.json is structured operator-facing card config that the AppCommander cockpit likely renders directly. If the operator confirms the cockpit doesn't consume either file (or if the operator is willing to accept that risk), they can be removed in a follow-up cut and appcommander/ disappears entirely. Beyond the two metadata files, the three Phase E4 feature follow-up threads the older hand-off had flagged are still available for a future session: the Phase D charter-amendment chain (new helpers in src/features/governance/ or src/features/connections/, brief lives in project-memory/foreman-memory/projects/tapit-wallet/briefs/ under a charter-amendment-chain-roadmap name), the JoinOrgModal vouch-cosignature collection sub-flow (extends src/features/cosigning/CosignRequestModal with an org-vouch-context variant alongside the existing org-action-context variant — chip-worthy because the picker shape differs), and the receiveSelfMembership orgSelfDecl-lookup centralization (small consistency cut to the create-attestation function family). HomeScreen.tsx sits at 797 lines, three lines under the 800-line hard limit — any further addition there will trigger the hard error and need an extraction up front (natural candidates: the inbox-routing dispatcher or one of the four tab-content renderers).
narrative.what_you_could_do_better: Two small observations. First, the operator's one-word 'Chips' directive landed without any framing about which chip they wanted, and I inferred from the prior carpenter's pre-loaded session.json that the appcommander/ cleanup was the obviously primed question. That inference was correct in the end — the operator picked the recommended option in one round-trip — but if the prior carpenter had left two competing chips in flight, 'Chips' would have been ambiguous and I would have had to ask the operator which one they meant, which itself is a chip. Worth naming as a pattern: when the prior session leaves more than one chip pre-loaded, the carpenter's first chip should be a meta-chip asking which of the pre-loaded chips to surface. The current session.json schema lets the prior carpenter rank pre-loaded chips by putting them in priority order inside next_session_starts_with, but it doesn't enforce that there be only one. Not worth a doctrine change yet but worth flagging if the pattern recurs. Second, the targeted-sweep commit deletes seventeen files but the diff is purely subtractive — no test changes, no doctrine changes, no schema migrations. That's exactly the shape a hygiene commit should have, but it does mean the close.sh hook's archive-idempotency check is now the only thing standing between this clean commit and the per-Stop checkpoint commit noise the prior session fixed. If the cmp -s ever fails to short-circuit (for any reason — a timestamp leak into session.json, a non-deterministic field, an encoding difference in the archive copy), the operator will see two commits per session instead of one. Worth a stress test in some future session where the carpenter deliberately re-Stops several times to confirm the idempotency holds across multiple Stop fires within one human-driven session.
narrative.bigger_picture: Two sessions ago the carpenter loop was a five-file comms protocol plus a hand-off letter plus two .mjs hook scripts plus a sprawling three-hundred-line doctrine block plus a stop-gate that raced fatally with the close hook plus a per-Stop checkpoint commit spam plus a sandbox-mode push bug that produced an infinite Stop-fire loop. As of this commit the carpenter loop is one JSON file plus two bash hooks plus a focused doctrine plus an empty-Stop short-circuit plus a working dispatch-branch push pattern — and the appcommander/ folder that carried the old loop's external scaffolding is down to two metadata files of unknown external readership. The reduction isn't glamorous because nothing user-facing shipped, but it is the substrate on which every future cut depends. The thesis here is that the carpenter loop should be the simplest thing that closes — fire up, ground, work, write the file, fire down — and that anything that doesn't fit that shape is friction the carpenter pays on every single session, multiplied across however many sessions ship across however many spawned projects across the fleet. Each removal in this two-commit arc (last session's hygiene cut plus this session's appcommander/ sweep) is paid back in carpenter wake-up time every session forever. The natural next move for the AppCommander side is to lift the entire two-commit arc into the skeleton template so future spawns inherit this loop from day one instead of starting in the old five-file world and having to migrate out of it the way this repo just did. That work belongs in COMMS_V2_AND_ADMIN_PAGE_SHIFT.md as concrete checklist items: rewrite skeleton CLAUDE.md doctrine block, strip session-start-grounding.mjs and session-stop-gate.mjs from skeleton-bundled scripts/, strip CARPENTER_HANDOFF.md from skeleton root, lift archive-idempotency cmp -s check into skeleton-bundled session-close.sh template, and remove the appcommander/scripts/carp-* and appcommander/peer-memory/* and appcommander/jobs/ and appcommander/manifests/ scaffolding from the skeleton wholesale.
